title: Genesis (band)
wiki_lead:
Genesis were an English rock band formed in 1967 at Charterhouse School in Godalming, Surrey. The band's longest-lasting and most commercially successful line-up consisted of keyboardist Tony Banks, bassist/guitarist Mike Rutherford and drummer/singer Phil Collins. In the 1970s, during which the band also included singer Peter Gabriel and guitarist Steve Hackett, Genesis were among the pioneers of progressive rock. With 100 million to 150 million albums sold worldwide, Genesis rank among the world's best-selling music artists. Their discography spans fifteen studio and six live albums. Their accolades include a Grammy Award for Best Concept Music Video for "Land of Confusion", and they were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2010. 
The band was formed by school pupils Banks, Rutherford, Gabriel, guitarist Anthony Phillips, and drummer Chris Stewart and were named by pop impresario and alumnus Jonathan King, who arranged the recording of several singles and their debut album From Genesis to Revelation (1969). After splitting from King, the band began touring, signed with Charisma Records, and shifted to progressive rock with their next album Trespass (1970). Phillips left the band and Banks, Rutherford and Gabriel recruited Collins and Hackett before recording Nursery Cryme (1971). Their live shows subsequently gained notoriety for Gabriel's theatrical costumes and performances. Foxtrot (1972) was their first charting album in the UK, while Selling England by the Pound (1973) reached number three and featured their first UK hit single, "I Know What I Like (In Your Wardrobe)". Gabriel left the group following a transatlantic tour for their concept double album, The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway (1974).
Collins took over as lead singer and, as a four-piece, the group released A Trick of the Tail and Wind & Wuthering (both 1976) with continued success. Hackett left the band in 1977, reducing the group to a three-piece of Banks, Rutherford and Collins. Their ninth studio album, ...And Then There Were Three... (1978), contained the band's first major hit, "Follow You Follow Me". Their next five studio albums – Duke (1980), Abacab (1981), Genesis (1983), Invisible Touch (1986) and We Can't Dance (1991) – saw the band embracing a more pop-oriented sound and achieving massive commercial success. Collins left Genesis in 1996 and was replaced by singer Ray Wilson for their final studio album, Calling All Stations (1997). Disappointing reception led the group to disband until Banks, Rutherford and Collins reunited for the Turn It On Again Tour in 2007 and The Last Domino? Tour in 2021.

grok_lead: Genesis is an English rock band formed in 1967 by schoolmates Tony Banks, Mike Rutherford, Peter Gabriel, Anthony Phillips, and Chris Stewart at Charterhouse School in Surrey. Initially emerging as a pioneering force in progressive rock during the early 1970s, the band gained acclaim for their intricate compositions, literary-inspired lyrics, and theatrical live performances led by frontman Peter Gabriel, with key additions including drummer Phil Collins in 1970 and guitarist Steve Hackett in 1971. Following Gabriel's departure in 1975, Collins assumed lead vocals. After guitarist Steve Hackett left in 1977, the remaining core trio of Banks (keyboards), Collins (vocals and drums), and Rutherford (guitars and bass) shifted toward a more radio-friendly pop-rock sound in the late 1970s and 1980s, achieving massive commercial success with albums such as Duke (1980), Abacab (1981), and especially Invisible Touch (1986), the latter featuring five US Top 10 singles (all Top 5) on the Billboard Hot 100 and becoming one of the best-selling albums worldwide. Over their career spanning more than five decades, Genesis released 15 studio albums, sold over 100 million records globally, and earned multiple certifications from the RIAA, including multi-platinum status for releases like Invisible Touch (6Ã Platinum in the U.S.), We Can't Dance (4Ã Platinum), and Genesis (4Ã Platinum), solidifying their influence across progressive, art, and mainstream rock genres. The band's evolution and the solo successes of members like Gabriel, Collins, and Hackett have cemented Genesis as one of the most enduring and commercially triumphant acts in rock history, with reunions and archival releases continuing to engage fans into the 2020s.
